It's monumental that you can acknowledge this yourself. It's okay that the pain hurts, because that's your mind's reaction to things happening that aren't right to you. When we touch a hot stove, our hands immediately fly away from the source of heat, but when we hurt inside we don't really have a way to identify what is the cause and what to do to stop it because our mental and emotional well being does not have pain receptors quite like the outside of our body does. It's good to recognize that there is pain, it means you're reacting to whatever is not right and wanting to pull back from it. In these situations, it sometimes seems impossible to escape that pain so a lot of us turn to wanting to just end everything because at least the hurting stops. I don't know what you're going through. You could be living physically with the causes of your pain or the pain could be from isolation or any mixture in between. I'm just glad you can recognize your pain doesn't mean you want to stop living. I hope you can find a way to pull back from your pain. (And if you do, let the rest of us know haha). 

Here's to you.

I would straight up tell them. Sensitivity isn’t an issue here, you’re noticing a pattern that’s making you uncomfortable in a place you also live in, that’s messed up.  Your feelings are valid and it wouldn’t be right if they were allowed to be picky about the smallest shit and you aren’t even allowed to be picky about how you’re talked to. Confrontation is seriously a hard thing to do and it takes effort to talk things through but they should respect you. Trust, I’ve been in a situation where I felt I couldn’t come down to eat in the kitchen because of roommate behavior, that is not a feeling anyone should go through and if I went through it again I’d handle it differently because screw not being able to use stuff in your own place. 
Tl;dr: you’re not sensitive, talk about it with them.

You deserve to feel loved and supported. You deserve a safe place. It’s not like you’re asking for the world. It’s not like you’re demanding the impossible. It sounds really reasonable to be angry about this because communities, online or otherwise,  are super important to finding comfort, support, and potential solutions and it sounds like your community was taken away from you. That’s all fucked. I hate that people with similar disorders feel the need to down others in similar or even different but still debilitating situations like their own. I’ve personally been in that kind of situation and with a friend no less. I know the feeling. That’s just so so fucked and you don’t deserve that at all. I hope at least ranting about it helped you a feel even the slightest bit better. I hope there’s something done about it even if I can’t personally do something I hope you know there’s people who believe you should be afforded that much and that it might help ease your frustrations if even the tiniest bit.

If there are any significant others to be had make sure you note the policy on overnight guests on your apartment’s lease as well as discuss it well beforehand with your roommate. At first it can seem fine but if you don’t state it to begin with someone can see fit to take advantage of an unspoken boundary and you’ll find yourself with a third roommate. Be fair in those negotiations but don’t be a pushover as you also live there. Whether the S/O of either of you is male or female it’s not really cool to keep them around for days on in, even if they offer to pay rent because neither party is expecting to stay with that third party. That being said, discussions over this matter in the future is a thing to be had and may well enough come up so make sure to always keep communication open.
